messages.subject: estimate the joint probability distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a data set with 10 binary variables and I want to estimate the
joint probability distribution. I want to use Bayesian networks to
simplify this probability distribution, as I expect several variables
to be independent. When I use the deal package, is it correct to
estimate the joint probability from the values of localprob() after
fitting a network (multiply these values), or can I just use my data
to estimate the local probabilities by assuming the dependency
structure that is found by the network? 

Thanks a lot in advance,
Christina

messages.subject: Simulating new individuals using a posterior network?
messages.subject_clean: Simulating new individuals using a posterior network?
messages.body_plain:
Hi ?deal? users

I have a network composed entirely of discrete nodes. After ?learning? from
a training data set, I want to use the conditional posterior probabilities
of each node to simulate a data set of ?fake? individuals. 

The reason for doing this is confidentiality. Potentially at least, I can
release a data set of ?fake? individuals for analysis by others, in situations
where I am not allowed to release real data because individuals could then
be identified.

There are some features in ?deal? that will help me do this ? the ?simprob?
property of each node, and the ?rnetwork? function. But the ?makesimprob?
function which sets the ?simprob? property creates uniform probabilities
for discrete nodes. 

So it seems as if I have to replace the uniform ?simprob? for each node with
its conditional posterior probability (found via the ?localprob? function?).
Then I can use the ?rnetwork? function. But this switching probabilities
is not as easy as it sounds, because these objects are different classes
and seem to represent each node using a different layout. [For example, for
a certain node ?simprob? is a 2x3 matrix whereas ?localprob? is a 3x2 table!]

Has anybody done this sort of thing before?

Best wishes Jim

messages.subject_clean: SV: Simulating new individuals using a posterior network?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jim

You might want to take a look at the demo called 'simulation',

library(deal)
demo(simulation)

I can't remember why the classes of simprob and localprob do not match. The 'localprob' came late in the implementation and was designed to fit with the 'Hugin' .net format. 

I have had reports, that localprob is not calculated properly for continuous nodes.

Best,
Claus

messages.subject: Re: estimate the joint probability distribution
messages.body_plain:
kikilalipuna <kikilalipuna <at> yahoo.de> writes:

> When I use the deal package, is it correct to
> estimate the joint probability from the values of localprob() after
> fitting a network (multiply these values)

Yes.

> , or can I just use my data
> to estimate the local probabilities by assuming the dependency
> structure that is found by the network? 

I would not do this, since the 'localprob's are calculated using prior 
information on the parameters as well as on the structure. I believe you should 
retain this information.

Best,
Claus
